subject: Dedicated capacity expansion: ops trade-offs & spill plan
messages:
From: Linh Tran <linh.tran@acme.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme.com>, ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity ask ahead of renewal — Q3 forecast attached

Hi Priya,

Hope you're well. We're pulling together numbers for our upcoming renewal and want to explore adding dedicated capacity on Day 1 of the new term. High-level ask below: 

- Baseline: add +30 GPUs to our reserved pool immediately at renewal.
- Requirement: 99th pct latency target at our peak (end of quarter runs).
- Concern: unpredictable spikes during launches — we need a safe overflow plan that doesn't blow the budget.

Attached is our Q2 demand forecast (acme_demand_forecast_q2.xlsx) and a short note on traffic shapes. Can you outline options for a) firm reserved increase, b) burst/on-demand spillover with cost guardrails, and c) an SLA that maps to throughput guarantees?

Thanks — would love a short call next week to align.

Linh
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Robotics

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Linh Tran <linh.tran@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask ahead of renewal — Q3 forecast attached

Hi Linh — thanks for the forecast and the clear asks. I'm looping in Dev and Karthik for the technical and commercial details. High-level options we typically offer (quick summary):

1) Reserved top-up (hard commit). 30 GPUs added to your pool. Predictable cost, priority scheduling, KV cache warm across workloads. Best when you want strict throughput guarantees.

2) Soft overflow (soft quota + burst credits). We keep your reserved pool but allow on-demand spillover above the commit. Spillover billed at a higher unit rate but with a monthly cost ceiling we can define. Easier to start smaller and avoid immediate capex.

3) Hybrid: partial top-up + smaller soft overflow band. Example: +20 reserved GPUs + up to 1.5x burst with a capped monthly charge.

Questions to help us size proposals before a call:
- What proportion of traffic is predictable vs sudden launches (pct)?
- Do you need a contractual p99 latency SLA or an operating-level target?
- Preferred term: 12 vs 24 months? Longer terms give us room to provide better base pricing and crediting for spillover.

I'll draft a proposal and a short MAP for the next steps. Can you do Wed 14th, 11am PT for a 30-min call?

Best,
Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Linh Tran <linh.tran@acme.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask ahead of renewal — Q3 forecast attached

Linh — quick technical note following Priya:

- Throughput/backpressure: a committed GPU capacity ensures reserved scheduling and persistent KV cache hotspots; on-demand spillover routes to our pooled on-demand fleet where cold-starts and quantization profiles may add ~5-15% latency variance.
- Latency SLA mapping: for guaranteed p99 we recommend the hard commit path. For soft overflow, we can provide an "operational target" with SLA only on the reserved portion.
- Autoscaling: we can implement a staged ramp (10% step every 30s) to avoid thundering herd. If you want stricter tail controls, we can enable a short-window rate limiter in front of the model route.

I've attached a short technical appendix with capacity breakpoints and expected tokens/sec per GPU for your workload (dedicated-expansion-options.pdf).

—Dev
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Linh Tran <linh.tran@acme.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme.com>, ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask ahead of renewal — Q3 forecast attached

Thanks Priya/Dev — helpful. A few clarifications from procurement & product: 

- We're inclined toward a hybrid: prefer lower initial commit (20 GPUs) plus burst for launches. Budget constraint: ~20-25% headroom on monthly run-rate for spillover.
- Term: procurement prefers 24 months if you can provide reasonable spillover credits/discounts.
- Commercial ask: can you show modeled pricing for (A) 12-month 30-GPU commit vs (B) 24-month 20-GPU commit + 1.5x burst soft overflow with a monthly cap?

If you can send a draft commercial term sheet and MAP, we can route to legal/procurement next week.

Linh

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Linh Tran <linh.tran@acme.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask ahead of renewal — Q3 forecast attached

Linh — attaching a commercial starter for the two scenarios (commercial-terms-draft.docx). Key points: 

- 12m / 30 GPUs: higher per-GPU rate, no spillover credits.
- 24m / 20 GPUs + 1.5x soft overflow: lower base rate; overflow billed at 1.5x base with a monthly overflow cap set at 25% of committed spend. We can add a burst-credit pool that exchanges unused reserved spend for burst credits at month-end (50% conversion).
- SLAs: guaranteed throughput and priority for reserved lanes; soft overflow gets best-effort with operational targets. We can commit to escalation SLOs for overflow incidents and a 30-day rollback window.

Laura — can you run the finance calc and confirm scaled ARR impact?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Linh Tran <linh.tran@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: MAP + proposed commitment 

Linh — thanks everyone for the input. Summary and proposed next steps: 

Summary of agreed preference:
- Acme preference: 24-month commitment for 20 reserved GPUs + soft overflow up to 1.5x of committed capacity.
- Pricing model: base rate for reserved GPUs (24m discount) + overflow billed at 1.5x unit price with a monthly cap of 25% of committed spend. Overflow credits: convert unused reserved spend into burst credits at 50% conversion at month close.
- SLA: reserved lanes carry p99 latency commitment; overflow is best-effort with incident escalation SLOs.

Action items:
1) Redwood: produce a consolidated commercial term sheet and a one-page MAP with timeline for legal/procurement (attached MAP-proposed-timeline.pdf).
2) Acme: confirm the preferred signatory and procurement lead for routing the 24m PO; share any required PO terms or procurement clauses.
3) Technical sync (optional): Dev to run a short smoke test on a staging burst to validate latency profiles.

Can we target a legal-ready term sheet by Tue Apr 26? I'll follow up with a shared Drive link for the final MAP.

Thanks — Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
